subject: Questions on Particle MCMC Methodology in nimbleSMC

messages.author: 01ee9baab3340811
messages.subject: Questions on Particle MCMC Methodology in nimbleSMC
parts:
Dear nimble users and developers,

I hope this message finds you well. I have two questions regarding the use of Particle MCMC and the specific definitions of this algorithm as outlined in the nimbleSMC paper (https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v100i03).

  1. Could you clarify the difference between Particle MCMC and particle marginal Metropolis-Hastings (PMMH) as discussed in this paper (Chapter 3.6, pp. 11–13)? Additionally, which of these corresponds to the RW_PF_block sampler in the nimble package?
  2. Am I correct in understanding that when using this methodology(maybe PMMH), there is no need to calculate or be concerned with the rhat value of latent variables? My interpretation is based on the statement in the paper, “If the latent states, x1:T​, are not needed as part of the PMMH output, the steps to track and record them can simply be skipped.” I will, of course, be checking the convergence of the top-level parameters, θ.

Thank you very much for your assistance and clarification.

Best regards,
Kei

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Questions on Particle MCMC Methodology in nimbleSMC
parts:
Dear Kei,

PMMH is a specific case of the more general idea of PMCMC (similarly to how MH is a specific approach to MCMC). 

Yes, the RW_PF_block sampler is using MH sampling for the non-state-space parameters, so that is PMMH.

Yes, the states are sampled from their conditional distribution and there should be no need to use convergence diagnostics for them.

Perry
